!=.doc: A is not equal to B => {0 or 1}

%.doc: A modulo B. Fail if B == 0.

&&.doc: A is not zero and B is not zero => {0 or 1}

*.doc: A times B. Fail on overflow.
*.extra: Overflow is an error condition which halts execution and fails the transaction. Full precision is available from `mulw`.

+.doc: A plus B. Fail on overflow.
+.extra: Overflow is an error condition which halts execution and fails the transaction. Full precision is available from `addw`.

-.doc: A minus B. Fail if B > A.

/.doc: A divided by B (truncated division). Fail if B == 0.
/.extra: `divmodw` is available to divide the two-element values produced by `mulw` and `addw`.

<=.doc: A less than or equal to B => {0 or 1}

==.doc: A is equal to B => {0 or 1}

>=.doc: A greater than or equal to B => {0 or 1}

acct_params_get.doc: X is field F from account A. Y is 1 if A owns positive algos, else 0

addw.doc: A plus B as a 128-bit result. X is the carry-bit, Y is the low-order 64 bits.

app_box_create.doc: create a box named B, of length C, for app A. Fail if the name B is empty or C exceeds 32,768. Returns 0 if B already existed, else 1
app_box_create.extra: Newly created boxes are filled with 0 bytes. `app_box_create` will fail if the referenced box already exists with a different size. Otherwise, existing boxes are unchanged by `app_box_create`.

app_box_del.doc: delete box named B of app A if it exists. Return 1 if B existed, 0 otherwise

app_box_extract.doc: read D bytes from box B of app A, starting at offset C. Fail if box B does not exist, or the byte range is outside B's size.

app_box_get.doc: X is the contents of box B of app A if B exists, else ''. Y is 1 if B exists, else 0.
app_box_get.extra: For boxes that exceed 4,096 bytes, consider `app_box_create`, `app_box_extract`, and `app_box_replace`

app_box_len.doc: X is the length of box B of app A if B exists, else 0. Y is 1 if B exists, else 0.

app_box_put.doc: replaces the contents of box B of app A with byte-array C. Fails if B exists and len(C) != len(box B). Creates B if it does not exist
app_box_put.extra: For boxes that exceed 4,096 bytes, consider `app_box_create`, `app_box_extract`, and `app_box_replace`

app_box_replace.doc: write byte-array D into box B of app A, starting at offset C. Fail if box B does not exist, or the byte range is outside B's size.

app_box_resize.doc: change the size of box named B of app A to be of length C, adding zero bytes to end or removing bytes from the end, as needed. Fail if the name B is empty, B is not an existing box, or C exceeds 32,768.

app_box_splice.doc: set box B of app A to contain its previous bytes up to index C, followed by E, followed by the original bytes of B that began at index C+D.
app_box_splice.extra: Boxes are of constant length. If D < len(E), then len(E)-D bytes will be removed from the end. If D > len(E), zero bytes will be appended to the end to reach the box length.

app_global_del.doc: delete key A from the global state of the current application
app_global_del.extra:
params: state key.



Deleting a key which is already absent has no effect on the application global state. (In particular, it does _not_ cause the program to fail.)

app_global_get.doc: global state of the key A in the current application
app_global_get.extra: params: state key. Return: value. The value is zero (of type uint64) if the key does not exist.

app_global_get_ex.doc: X is the global state of application A, key B. Y is 1 if key existed, else 0
app_global_get_ex.extra: params: Txn.ForeignApps offset (or, since v4, an _available_ application id), state key. Return: did_exist flag (top of the stack, 1 if the application and key existed and 0 otherwise), value. The value is zero (of type uint64) if the key does not exist.

app_global_put.doc: write B to key A in the global state of the current application

app_local_del.doc: delete key B from account A's local state of the current application
app_local_del.extra:
params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), state key.



Deleting a key which is already absent has no effect on the application local state. (In particular, it does _not_ cause the program to fail.)

app_local_get.doc: local state of the key B in the current application in account A
app_local_get.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), state key. Return: value. The value is zero (of type uint64) if the key does not exist.

app_local_get_ex.doc: X is the local state of application B, key C in account A. Y is 1 if key existed, else 0
app_local_get_ex.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), _available_ application id (or, since v4, a Txn.ForeignApps offset), state key. Return: did_exist flag (top of the stack, 1 if the application and key existed and 0 otherwise), value. The value is zero (of type uint64) if the key does not exist.

app_local_put.doc: write C to key B in account A's local state of the current application
app_local_put.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), state key, value.

app_opted_in.doc: 1 if account A is opted in to application B, else 0
app_opted_in.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), _available_ application id (or, since v4, a Txn.ForeignApps offset). Return: 1 if opted in and 0 otherwise.

app_params_get.doc: X is field F from app A. Y is 1 if A exists, else 0
app_params_get.extra: params: Txn.ForeignApps offset or an _available_ app id. Return: did_exist flag (1 if the application existed and 0 otherwise), value.

app_params_set.doc: set field F of the current app to A

assert.doc: immediately fail unless A is a non-zero number

asset_holding_get.doc: X is field F from account A's holding of asset B. Y is 1 if A is opted into B, else 0
asset_holding_get.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ address), asset id (or, since v4, a Txn.ForeignAssets offset). Return: did_exist flag (1 if the asset existed and 0 otherwise), value.

asset_params_get.doc: X is field F from asset A. Y is 1 if A exists, else 0
asset_params_get.extra: params: Txn.ForeignAssets offset (or, since v4, an _available_ asset id. Return: did_exist flag (1 if the asset existed and 0 otherwise), value.

b.extra: See `bnz` for details on how branches work. `b` always jumps to the offset.

b!=.doc: 0 if A is equal to B, else 1. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b%.doc: A modulo B. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers. Fail if B is zero.

b&.doc: A bitwise-and B. A and B are zero-left extended to the greater of their lengths

b*.doc: A times B. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers.

b+.doc: A plus B. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b-.doc: A minus B. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers. Fail on underflow.

b/.doc: A divided by B (truncated division). A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers. Fail if B is zero.

b<.doc: 1 if A is less than B, else 0. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b<=.doc: 1 if A is less than or equal to B, else 0. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b==.doc: 1 if A is equal to B, else 0. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b>.doc: 1 if A is greater than B, else 0. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b>=.doc: 1 if A is greater than or equal to B, else 0. A and B are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

b^.doc: A bitwise-xor B. A and B are zero-left extended to the greater of their lengths

balance.doc: balance for account A, in microalgos. The balance is observed after the effects of previous transactions in the group, and after the fee for the current transaction is deducted. Changes caused by inner transactions are observable immediately following `itxn_submit`
balance.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), _available_ application id (or, since v4, a Txn.ForeignApps offset). Return: value.

base64_decode.doc: decode A which was base64-encoded using _encoding_ E. Fail if A is not base64 encoded with encoding E
base64_decode.extra:
_Warning_: Usage should be restricted to very rare use cases. In almost all cases, smart contracts should directly handle non-encoded byte-strings. This opcode should only be used in cases where base64 is the only available option, e.g. interoperability with a third-party that only signs base64 strings.



 Decodes A using the base64 encoding E. Specify the encoding with an immediate arg either as URL and Filename Safe (`URLEncoding`) or Standard (`StdEncoding`). See [RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5](https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html#section-4). It is assumed that the encoding ends with the exact number of `=` padding characters as required by the RFC. When padding occurs, any unused pad bits in the encoding must be set to zero or the decoding will fail. The special cases of `\n` and `\r` are allowed but completely ignored. An error will result when attempting to decode a string with a character that is not in the encoding alphabet or not one of `=`, `\r`, or `\n`.

bitlen.doc: The highest set bit in A. If A is a byte-array, it is interpreted as a big-endian unsigned integer. bitlen of 0 is 0, bitlen of 8 is 4
bitlen.extra: bitlen interprets arrays as big-endian integers, unlike setbit/getbit

block.doc: field F of block A. Fail unless A falls between txn.LastValid-1002 and txn.FirstValid (exclusive)

bmodexp.doc: A to the power of B, modulo C. A, B and C are big-endian unsigned integers of up to 4096 bytes. Fails if C is zero, or if A and B are both zero.
bmodexp.cost: 10 + 1 per 32 bytes of A, B and C, plus more depending on the size of B and C

bnz.doc: branch to TARGET if value A is not zero
bnz.extra:
The `bnz` instruction opcode 0x40 is followed by two immediate data bytes which are a high byte first and low byte second which together form a 16 bit offset which the instruction may branch to. For a bnz instruction at `pc`, if the last element of the stack is not zero then branch to instruction at `pc + 3 + N`, else proceed to next instruction at `pc + 3`. Branch targets must be aligned instructions. (e.g. Branching to the second byte of a 2 byte op will be rejected.) Starting at v4, the offset is treated as a signed 16 bit integer allowing for backward branches and looping. In prior version (v1 to v3), branch offsets are limited to forward branches only, 0-0x7fff.



At v2 it became allowed to branch to the end of the program exactly after the last instruction: bnz to byte N (with 0-indexing) was illegal for a TEAL program with N bytes before v2, and is legal after it. This change eliminates the need for a last instruction of no-op as a branch target at the end. (Branching beyond the end--in other words, to a byte larger than N--is still illegal and will cause the program to fail.)

box_create.doc: create a box named A, of length B. Fail if the name A is empty or B exceeds 32,768. Returns 0 if A already existed, else 1
box_create.extra: Newly created boxes are filled with 0 bytes. `box_create` will fail if the referenced box already exists with a different size. Otherwise, existing boxes are unchanged by `box_create`.

box_del.doc: delete box named A if it exists. Return 1 if A existed, 0 otherwise

box_extract.doc: read C bytes from box A, starting at offset B. Fail if A does not exist, or the byte range is outside A's size.

box_get.doc: X is the contents of box A if A exists, else ''. Y is 1 if A exists, else 0.
box_get.extra: For boxes that exceed 4,096 bytes, consider `box_create`, `box_extract`, and `box_replace`

box_len.doc: X is the length of box A if A exists, else 0. Y is 1 if A exists, else 0.

box_put.doc: replaces the contents of box A with byte-array B. Fails if A exists and len(B) != len(box A). Creates A if it does not exist
box_put.extra: For boxes that exceed 4,096 bytes, consider `box_create`, `box_extract`, and `box_replace`

box_replace.doc: write byte-array C into box A, starting at offset B. Fail if A does not exist, or the byte range is outside A's size.

box_resize.doc: change the size of box named A to be of length B, adding zero bytes to end or removing bytes from the end, as needed. Fail if the name A is empty, A is not an existing box, or B exceeds 32,768.

box_splice.doc: set box A to contain its previous bytes up to index B, followed by D, followed by the original bytes of A that began at index B+C.
box_splice.extra: Boxes are of constant length. If C < len(D), then len(D)-C bytes will be removed from the end. If C > len(D), zero bytes will be appended to the end to reach the box length.

bsqrt.doc: The largest integer I such that I^2 <= A. A and I are interpreted as big-endian unsigned integers

btoi.doc: converts big-endian byte array A to uint64. Fails if len(A) > 8. Padded by leading 0s if len(A) < 8.
btoi.extra: `btoi` fails if the input is longer than 8 bytes.

bury.doc: replace the Nth value from the top of the stack with A. bury 0 fails.

imm: a block of byte constant values
bytecblock.doc: prepare block of byte-array constants for use by bytec
bytecblock.extra: `bytecblock` loads the following program bytes into an array of byte-array constants in the evaluator. These constants can be referred to by `bytec` and `bytec_*` which will push the value onto the stack. Subsequent calls to `bytecblock` reset and replace the bytes constants available to the script.

bz.doc: branch to TARGET if value A is zero
bz.extra: See `bnz` for details on how branches work. `bz` inverts the behavior of `bnz`.

bzero.doc: zero filled byte-array of length A

b|.doc: A bitwise-or B. A and B are zero-left extended to the greater of their lengths

callsub.doc: branch unconditionally to TARGET, saving the next instruction on the call stack
callsub.extra: The call stack is separate from the data stack. Only `callsub`, `retsub`, and `proto` manipulate it.

concat.extra: `concat` fails if the result would be greater than 4096 bytes.

cover.doc: remove top of stack, and place it deeper in the stack such that N elements are above it. Fails if stack depth <= N.

dig.doc: Nth value from the top of the stack. dig 0 is equivalent to dup

divmodw.extra: The notation J,K indicates that two uint64 values J and K are interpreted as a uint128 value, with J as the high uint64 and K the low.

divw.doc: A,B / C. Fail if C == 0 or if result overflows.
divw.extra: The notation A,B indicates that A and B are interpreted as a uint128 value, with A as the high uint64 and B the low.

ec_add.doc: for curve points A and B, return the curve point A + B
ec_add.extra:
A and B are curve points in affine representation: field element X concatenated with field element Y. Field element `Z` is encoded as follows.

For the base field elements (Fp), `Z` is encoded as a big-endian number and must be lower than the field modulus.

For the quadratic field extension (Fp2), `Z` is encoded as the concatenation of the individual encoding of the coefficients. For an Fp2 element of the form `Z = Z0 + Z1 i`, where `i` is a formal quadratic non-residue, the encoding of Z is the concatenation of the encoding of `Z0` and `Z1` in this order. (`Z0` and `Z1` must be less than the field modulus).



The point at infinity is encoded as `(X,Y) = (0,0)`.

Groups G1 and G2 are denoted additively.



Fails if A or B is not in G.

A and/or B are allowed to be the point at infinity.

Does _not_ check if A and B are in the main prime-order subgroup.

ec_map_to.doc: maps field element A to group G
ec_map_to.extra:
BN254 points are mapped by the SVDW map. BLS12-381 points are mapped by the SSWU map.

G1 element inputs are base field elements and G2 element inputs are quadratic field elements, with nearly the same encoding rules (for field elements) as defined in `ec_add`. There is one difference of encoding rule: G1 element inputs do not need to be 0-padded if they fit in less than 32 bytes for BN254 and less than 48 bytes for BLS12-381. (As usual, the empty byte array represents 0.) G2 elements inputs need to be always have the required size.

ec_multi_scalar_mul.doc: for curve points A and scalars B, return curve point B0A0 + B1A1 + B2A2 + ... + BnAn
ec_multi_scalar_mul.cost: BN254g1=3600 + 90 per 32 bytes of B; BN254g2=7200 + 270 per 32 bytes of B; BLS12_381g1=6500 + 95 per 32 bytes of B; BLS12_381g2=14850 + 485 per 32 bytes of B
ec_multi_scalar_mul.extra:
A is a list of concatenated points, encoded and checked as described in `ec_add`. B is a list of concatenated scalars which, unlike ec_scalar_mul, must all be exactly 32 bytes long.

The name `ec_multi_scalar_mul` was chosen to reflect common usage, but a more consistent name would be `ec_multi_scalar_mul`. AVM values are limited to 4096 bytes, so `ec_multi_scalar_mul` is limited by the size of the points in the group being operated upon.

ec_pairing_check.doc: 1 if the product of the pairing of each point in A with its respective point in B is equal to the identity element of the target group Gt, else 0
ec_pairing_check.cost: BN254g1=8000 + 7400 per 64 bytes of B; BN254g2=8000 + 7400 per 128 bytes of B; BLS12_381g1=13000 + 10000 per 96 bytes of B; BLS12_381g2=13000 + 10000 per 192 bytes of B
ec_pairing_check.extra: A and B are concatenated points, encoded and checked as described in `ec_add`. A contains points of the group G, B contains points of the associated group (G2 if G is G1, and vice versa). Fails if A and B have a different number of points, or if any point is not in its described group or outside the main prime-order subgroup - a stronger condition than other opcodes. AVM values are limited to 4096 bytes, so `ec_pairing_check` is limited by the size of the points in the groups being operated upon.

ec_scalar_mul.doc: for curve point A and scalar B, return the curve point BA, the point A multiplied by the scalar B.
ec_scalar_mul.extra: A is a curve point encoded and checked as described in `ec_add`. Scalar B is interpreted as a big-endian unsigned integer. Fails if B exceeds 32 bytes.

ec_subgroup_check.doc: 1 if A is in the main prime-order subgroup of G (including the point at infinity) else 0. Program fails if A is not in G at all.

ecdsa_pk_decompress.doc: decompress pubkey A into components X, Y
ecdsa_pk_decompress.extra: The 33 byte public key in a compressed form to be decompressed into X and Y (top) components. All values are big-endian encoded.

ecdsa_pk_recover.doc: for (data A, recovery id B, signature C, D) recover a public key
ecdsa_pk_recover.extra: S (top) and R elements of a signature, recovery id and data (bottom) are expected on the stack and used to deriver a public key. All values are big-endian encoded. The signed data must be 32 bytes long.

ecdsa_verify.doc: for (data A, signature B, C and pubkey D, E) verify the signature of the data against the pubkey => {0 or 1}
ecdsa_verify.extra: The 32 byte Y-component of a public key is the last element on the stack, preceded by X-component of a pubkey, preceded by S and R components of a signature, preceded by the data that is fifth element on the stack. All values are big-endian encoded. The signed data must be 32 bytes long, and signatures in lower-S form are only accepted.

ed25519verify.doc: for (data A, signature B, pubkey C) verify the signature of ("ProgData" || program_hash || data) against the pubkey => {0 or 1}
ed25519verify.extra: The 32 byte public key is the last element on the stack, preceded by the 64 byte signature at the second-to-last element on the stack, preceded by the data which was signed at the third-to-last element on the stack.

ed25519verify_bare.doc: for (data A, signature B, pubkey C) verify the signature of the data against the pubkey => {0 or 1}

exp.doc: A raised to the Bth power. Fail if A == B == 0 and on overflow

expw.doc: A raised to the Bth power as a 128-bit result in two uint64s. X is the high 64 bits, Y is the low. Fail if A == B == 0 or if the results exceeds 2^128-1

extract.doc: A range of bytes from A starting at S up to but not including S+L. If L is 0, then extract to the end of the string. If S or S+L is larger than the array length, the program fails

extract3.doc: A range of bytes from A starting at B up to but not including B+C. If B+C is larger than the array length, the program fails

extract_uint16.doc: A uint16 formed from a range of big-endian bytes from A starting at B up to but not including B+2. If B+2 is larger than the array length, the program fails

extract_uint32.doc: A uint32 formed from a range of big-endian bytes from A starting at B up to but not including B+4. If B+4 is larger than the array length, the program fails

extract_uint64.doc: A uint64 formed from a range of big-endian bytes from A starting at B up to but not including B+8. If B+8 is larger than the array length, the program fails

falcon_verify.doc: for (data A, deterministic FALCON-1024 compressed-format signature B, pubkey C) verify the signature of data against the pubkey => {0 or 1}
falcon_verify.extra: Signature B is variable-length, with maximum size 1423 bytes.

frame_bury.doc: replace the Nth (signed) value from the frame pointer in the stack with A

frame_dig.doc: Nth (signed) value from the frame pointer.

gaid.doc: ID of the asset or application created in the Tth transaction of the current group
gaid.extra: `gaid` fails unless the requested transaction created an asset or application and T < GroupIndex.

gaids.doc: ID of the asset or application created in the Ath transaction of the current group
gaids.extra: `gaids` fails unless the requested transaction created an asset or application and A < GroupIndex.

getbit.doc: Bth bit of (byte-array or integer) A. If B is greater than or equal to the bit length of the value (8*byte length), the program fails
getbit.extra: see explanation of bit ordering in setbit

getbyte.doc: Bth byte of A, as an integer. If B is greater than or equal to the array length, the program fails

gitxn.doc: field F of the Tth transaction in the last inner group submitted

gitxna.doc: Ith value of the array field F from the Tth transaction in the last inner group submitted

gitxnas.doc: Ath value of the array field F from the Tth transaction in the last inner group submitted

imm: position in scratch space to load from
gload.doc: Ith scratch space value of the Tth transaction in the current group
gload.extra: `gload` fails unless the requested transaction is an ApplicationCall and T < GroupIndex.

imm: position in scratch space to load from
gloads.doc: Ith scratch space value of the Ath transaction in the current group
gloads.extra: `gloads` fails unless the requested transaction is an ApplicationCall and A < GroupIndex.

gloadss.doc: Bth scratch space value of the Ath transaction in the current group

gtxn.doc: field F of the Tth transaction in the current group
gtxn.extra: for notes on transaction fields available, see `txn`. If this transaction is _i_ in the group, `gtxn i field` is equivalent to `txn field`.

gtxna.doc: Ith value of the array field F from the Tth transaction in the current group

gtxnas.doc: Ath value of the array field F from the Tth transaction in the current group

gtxns.doc: field F of the Ath transaction in the current group
gtxns.extra: for notes on transaction fields available, see `txn`. If top of stack is _i_, `gtxns field` is equivalent to `gtxn _i_ field`. gtxns exists so that _i_ can be calculated, often based on the index of the current transaction.

gtxnsa.doc: Ith value of the array field F from the Ath transaction in the current group

gtxnsas.doc: Bth value of the array field F from the Ath transaction in the current group

imm: a block of int constant values
intcblock.doc: prepare block of uint64 constants for use by intc
intcblock.extra: `intcblock` loads following program bytes into an array of integer constants in the evaluator. These integer constants can be referred to by `intc` and `intc_*` which will push the value onto the stack. Subsequent calls to `intcblock` reset and replace the integer constants available to the script.

itob.doc: converts uint64 A to big-endian byte array, always of length 8

itxn.doc: field F of the last inner transaction

itxn_begin.doc: begin preparation of a new inner transaction in a new transaction group
itxn_begin.extra: `itxn_begin` initializes Sender to the application address; Fee to the minimum allowable, taking into account MinTxnFee and credit from overpaying in earlier transactions; FirstValid/LastValid to the values in the invoking transaction, and all other fields to zero or empty values.

itxn_field.doc: set field F of the current inner transaction to A
itxn_field.extra: `itxn_field` fails if A is of the wrong type for F, including a byte array of the wrong size for use as an address when F is an address field. `itxn_field` also fails if A is an account, asset, or app that is not _available_, or an attempt is made extend an array field beyond the limit imposed by consensus parameters. (Addresses set into asset params of acfg transactions need not be _available_.)

itxn_next.doc: begin preparation of a new inner transaction in the same transaction group
itxn_next.extra: `itxn_next` initializes the transaction exactly as `itxn_begin` does

itxn_submit.doc: execute the current inner transaction group. Fail if executing this group would exceed the inner transaction limit, or if any transaction in the group fails.
itxn_submit.extra: `itxn_submit` resets the current transaction so that it can not be resubmitted. A new `itxn_begin` is required to prepare another inner transaction.

itxna.doc: Ith value of the array field F of the last inner transaction

itxnas.doc: Ath value of the array field F of the last inner transaction

json_ref.doc: key B's value, of type R, from a [valid](jsonspec.md) utf-8 encoded json object A
json_ref.extra:
_Warning_: Usage should be restricted to very rare use cases, as JSON decoding is expensive and quite limited. In addition, JSON objects are large and not optimized for size.



Almost all smart contracts should use simpler and smaller methods (such as the [ABI](https://arc.algorand.foundation/ARCs/arc-0004). This opcode should only be used in cases where JSON is only available option, e.g. when a third-party only signs JSON.

keccak256.doc: Keccak256 hash of value A, yields [32]byte

len.doc: yields length of byte value A

imm: position in scratch space to load from
load.doc: Ith scratch space value. All scratch spaces are 0 at program start.

loads.doc: Ath scratch space value.  All scratch spaces are 0 at program start.

log.doc: write A to log state of the current application
log.extra: `log` fails if called more than MaxLogCalls times in a program, or if the sum of logged bytes exceeds 1024 bytes.

match.doc: given match cases from A[1] to A[N], branch to the Ith label where A[I] = B. Continue to the following instruction if no matches are found.
match.extra: `match` consumes N+1 values from the stack. Let the top stack value be B. The following N values represent an ordered list of match cases/constants (A), where the first value (A[0]) is the deepest in the stack. The immediate arguments are an ordered list of N labels (T). `match` will branch to target T[I], where A[I] = B. If there are no matches then execution continues on to the next instruction.

mimc.doc: MiMC hash of scalars A, using curve and parameters specified by configuration C
mimc.cost: BN254Mp110=10 + 550 per 32 bytes of A; BLS12_381Mp111=10 + 550 per 32 bytes of A
mimc.extra:
A is a non-empty list of concatenated 32 byte big-endian unsigned integer scalars.  Fail if A's length is not a multiple of 32 or any element is greater than or equal to the scalar field modulus.



MiMC hashes field elements, not arbitrary byte strings; reducing external inputs modulo the scalar field modulus makes congruent inputs hash identically. MiMC is thus not a general purpose hash function, but meant to be used in zero knowledge applications to match a zk-circuit implementation.

min_balance.doc: minimum required balance for account A, in microalgos. Required balance is affected by ASA, App, and Box usage. When creating or opting into an app, the minimum balance grows before the app code runs, therefore the increase is visible there. When deleting or closing out, the minimum balance decreases after the app executes. Changes caused by inner transactions or box usage are observable immediately following the opcode effecting the change.
min_balance.extra: params: Txn.Accounts offset (or, since v4, an _available_ account address), _available_ application id (or, since v4, a Txn.ForeignApps offset). Return: value.

mldsa_verify.doc: 1 if B is a valid ML-DSA (FIPS 204) signature of data A by public key C, with context D (empty for the default context), else 0.
mldsa_verify.extra: MLDSA44 takes a 2420 byte signature and a 1312 byte public key; MLDSA65 a 3309 byte signature and a 1952 byte public key. The context is at most 255 bytes.
mldsa_verify.cost: MLDSA44=3700 + 5 per 64 bytes of A; MLDSA65=5850 + 5 per 64 bytes of A

mulw.doc: A times B as a 128-bit result in two uint64s. X is the high 64 bits, Y is the low

online_stake.doc: the total online stake in the agreement round

popn.doc: remove N values from the top of the stack

poseidon2.doc: Poseidon2 hash of scalars A, using curve and parameters specified by configuration C
poseidon2.cost: BN254t2=7 + 350 per 32 bytes of A; BLS12_381t2=7 + 350 per 32 bytes of A
poseidon2.extra:
A is a non-empty list of concatenated 32 byte big-endian unsigned integer scalars. Fail if A's length is not a multiple of 32 or any element is greater than or equal to the scalar field modulus.



Poseidon2 hashes field elements, not arbitrary byte strings; reducing external inputs modulo the scalar field modulus makes congruent inputs hash identically. Poseidon2 is thus not a general purpose hash function, but meant to be used in zero knowledge applications to match a zk-circuit implementation.

proto.doc: Prepare top call frame for a retsub that will assume A args and R return values.
proto.extra: Fails unless the last instruction executed was a `callsub`.

pushbytes.extra: pushbytes args are not added to the bytecblock during assembly processes

pushbytess.doc: push sequences of immediate byte arrays to stack (first byte array being deepest)
pushbytess.extra: pushbytess args are not added to the bytecblock during assembly processes

pushint.extra: pushint args are not added to the intcblock during assembly processes

pushints.doc: push sequence of immediate uints to stack in the order they appear (first uint being deepest)
pushints.extra: pushints args are not added to the intcblock during assembly processes

replace2.doc: Copy of A with the bytes starting at S replaced by the bytes of B. Fails if S+len(B) exceeds len(A)

replace3.doc: Copy of A with the bytes starting at B replaced by the bytes of C. Fails if B+len(C) exceeds len(A)

retsub.doc: pop the top instruction from the call stack and branch to it
retsub.extra: If the current frame was prepared by `proto A R`, `retsub` will remove the 'A' arguments from the stack, move the `R` return values down, and pop any stack locations above the relocated return values.

return.doc: use A as success value; end

select.doc: selects one of two values based on top-of-stack: B if C != 0, else A

setbit.doc: Copy of (byte-array or integer) A, with the Bth bit set to (0 or 1) C. If B is greater than or equal to the bit length of the value (8*byte length), the program fails
setbit.extra: When A is a uint64, index 0 is the least significant bit. Setting bit 3 to 1 on the integer 0 yields 8, or 2^3. When A is a byte array, index 0 is the leftmost bit of the leftmost byte. Setting bits 0 through 11 to 1 in a 4-byte-array of 0s yields the byte array 0xfff00000. Setting bit 3 to 1 on the 1-byte-array 0x00 yields the byte array 0x10.

setbyte.doc: Copy of A with the Bth byte set to small integer (between 0..255) C. If B is greater than or equal to the array length, the program fails

sha256.doc: SHA256 hash of value A, yields [32]byte

sha3_256.doc: SHA3_256 hash of value A, yields [32]byte

sha512_256.doc: SHA512_256 hash of value A, yields [32]byte

sqrt.doc: The largest integer I such that I^2 <= A

imm: position in scratch space to store to
store.doc: store A to the Ith scratch space

stores.doc: store B to the Ath scratch space

substring.doc: A range of bytes from A starting at S up to but not including E. If E < S, or either is larger than the array length, the program fails

substring3.doc: A range of bytes from A starting at B up to but not including C. If C < B, or either is larger than the array length, the program fails

swap.doc: swaps A and B on stack

switch.doc: branch to the Ath label. Continue at following instruction if index A exceeds the number of labels.

txna.doc: Ith value of the array field F of the current transaction

txnas.doc: Ath value of the array field F of the current transaction

uncover.doc: remove the value at depth N in the stack and shift above items down so the Nth deep value is on top of the stack. Fails if stack depth <= N.

voter_params_get.doc: X is field F from online account A as of the balance round: 320 rounds before the current round. Y is 1 if A had positive algos online in the agreement round, else Y is 0 and X is a type specific zero-value

vrf_verify.doc: Verify the proof B of message A against pubkey C. Returns vrf output and verification flag.
vrf_verify.extra: `VrfAlgorand` is the VRF used in Algorand. It is ECVRF-ED25519-SHA512-Elligator2, specified in the IETF internet draft [draft-irtf-cfrg-vrf-03](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-vrf/03/).

||.doc: A is not zero or B is not zero => {0 or 1}
